description: A focused information pack for cystic fibrosis, CFTR biology, respiratory and digestive care, research, clinical trials and life with the condition. It is an information-discovery aid, not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited condition caused by changes in the CFTR gene. Abnormal CFTR protein affects salt and water movement, producing thick, sticky mucus that can affect the lungs, digestive system and other organs.
synopsis.manifestations: CF commonly involves persistent cough, recurrent chest infections, wheeze, breathlessness, reduced lung function and difficulty clearing mucus. It may also cause pancreatic insufficiency, digestive symptoms, poor growth, CF-related diabetes, liver disease, infertility in many men and other complications; presentation varies widely.
synopsis.management: Care is coordinated by specialist teams and may include airway-clearance techniques, inhaled medicines, antibiotics when indicated, CFTR modulator medicines for eligible variants, pancreatic enzymes, nutrition support, exercise and monitoring of complications. Some people with advanced lung disease may be assessed for transplantation.
synopsis.outlook: CF is lifelong and variable. Advances in diagnosis, infection treatment, nutrition, specialist care and CFTR modulators have improved outcomes for many people, but complications and access to effective therapies differ. An individual outlook should be discussed with the CF care team.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered cystic-fibrosis studies, including trials of CFTR modulators, infection treatments, airway clearance, nutrition, gene or mRNA therapies and monitoring. A listing does not indicate eligibility or recommendation.

topics.heading: Treatment and care
topics.description: Medicines and specialist care for airway clearance, infections, CFTR variants, digestion, nutrition, diabetes and other complications.

termDefinitions.CFTR modulator: A medicine designed to improve the function, amount or processing of altered CFTR protein for people with particular variants.
termDefinitions.airway clearance: Techniques and treatments used to move mucus out of the lungs.
termDefinitions.pancreatic enzyme replacement: Prescribed digestive enzymes used when pancreatic insufficiency reduces digestion or nutrient absorption.
termDefinitions.pulmonary exacerbation: A sustained worsening of respiratory symptoms or lung function that may require additional assessment or treatment.
termDefinitions.lung transplant: A major operation replacing diseased lungs for a small group with advanced lung disease.

topics.heading: Research and innovation
topics.description: Laboratory, translational and clinical research on CFTR biology, infection, inflammation, lung repair, gene and mRNA therapies, medicines and long-term outcomes.

topics.heading: Genetics and testing
topics.description: CFTR inheritance, variant testing, newborn screening, carrier testing and precision treatment; genetic results require qualified interpretation.

termDefinitions.CFTR: The gene that provides instructions for a protein regulating salt and water movement across cell surfaces; disease-causing variants can cause cystic fibrosis.
termDefinitions.CFTR variant: A change in the CFTR gene; its clinical significance depends on the specific variant and clinical context.
termDefinitions.autosomal recessive: An inheritance pattern in which a person generally needs disease-causing variants in both copies of a gene to have the condition.

topics.heading: Living with cystic fibrosis
topics.description: Daily life, respiratory health, nutrition, exercise, school, work, mental wellbeing, relationships, fertility, transitions and practical support for people living with CF.

topics.heading: Family and caregiving
topics.description: Information for parents, families, care partners and support networks, including treatment routines, infection precautions, education, emotional support and care coordination.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Patient organisations, public policy, equitable access to specialist care and medicines, disability inclusion, research participation, awareness and community support.
